# Maintaining the AI Configuration (stdagent)

This is the workflow for changing the AI rules of this repo. It was moved out of the root overview
(`.stdai/standards/root.md`) and the git-commit rule so the always-loaded rules stay small. Read it
before touching anything under `.stdai/standards/`, before editing a file that looks like a rule but
might be a generated artifact, or when you need to know which target produces which output path.

## Sources and generated outputs

AI rules are managed by stdagent. The sources live in `.stdai/standards/`; the generated outputs are
produced mechanically by `stdagent sync` and **MUST NOT be edited by hand**:

- claude-code target -> `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/commands/`, `.claude/skills/`
- codex target -> `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills/`

Workflow:

- Enabled targets: claude-code + codex (see `.stdai/config.toml`).
- Add / change / remove a rule: edit `.stdai/standards/<type>/<name>.md`, then run `stdagent sync`.
- Change this overview (tech stack, iron rules): edit `.stdai/standards/root.md`, then run
  `stdagent sync`.
- Check drift: `stdagent status`. Clean up stale outputs: `stdagent clean`.
- Generated outputs MUST be committed so that code review and PRs show AI rule changes. They are
  excluded from Oxfmt (root `vite.config.ts` `fmt.ignorePatterns`) so formatting never fights
  `stdagent sync`.

## Committing generated AI configuration

`stdagent sync` mechanically generates `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/skills/`,
`.claude/commands/`, and `.agents/skills/` from the sources in `.stdai/standards/`. These generated
files are tracked on purpose and MUST be committed alongside the source change, so review and pull
requests can see how the AI rules changed. Never edit a generated file directly, and never add one
to `.gitignore`.
